# Security

This layer manages signed, short-lived tokens for the setup page, ensuring secure communication and authentication.

## Overview

The Security layer is responsible for generating and validating tokens used in the setup page. These tokens are signed with a secret key derived from the `WEBHOOK_SECRET` environment variable, ensuring that they are tamper-proof and valid for a limited time.

## Responsibilities

- Generate and validate tokens for the setup page.
- Ensure secure communication and authentication.

## Key components

| File | Purpose | Main definitions |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [`app/src/session.ts`](../app/src/session.ts) | Manages signed, short-lived tokens for the setup page. | `TokenPurpose`, `signToken`, `verifyToken`, `randomToken`, `sameToken`, `base64url` |

## How it works

The Security layer uses HMAC-SHA256 to sign and verify tokens. Tokens consist of a purpose, an expiration time, and data, all encoded in base64url. The signing key is derived from the `WEBHOOK_SECRET` environment variable.

## Configuration

This layer does not require any additional configuration. It reads the `WEBHOOK_SECRET` environment variable to derive the signing key.
